text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Al Leach unveils megacity plan: Ontario puts financial curbs on six municipalities, regional government.
- 48-hour shelter rule proposed: Send battered women home quickly, report to province advises.
- Gilles Duceppe to run for top Bloc Quebecois job: MP expected to be front runner, has close ties to Bouchard.
- Red Cross workers assassinated: Canadian among six slain in Chechnya.
- Zap! Nintendo 64 vanishes from stores: As demand rises, so does the price; bidding has reached $1,500 for a system that originally sold for $279.
- Husky plans new megaproject: Leads group with $1.5 billion strategy to tap huge Whiterose oil field in North Atlantic.
- Peter Pocklington pulls plug on Canbra Foods bid: Lender's refusal kills deal, sending shares down $7.45.
- AT&T Canada given option on phone stake: Royal could quit long-distance firm.
- Mortgage rates inch upward: Selloff in debt markets prompts Canada Trust's increase.
- Placer bid back on track: Takeover target Highlands Gold removes legal obstacles to US$340 million bid and acquisition-hungry Placer Dome raises its cash reserve to US$1.4 billion.
- Bank's resistance kills Pocklington bid for Canbra.
